findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show existing electric easement boundaries with dimensions from easement boundaries to proposed structures. The site plan and grading plan show easement locations but provide no dimensioned clearances. Please provide a clearance exhibit dimensioning the separation between recorded electric easement boundaries and all structures, driveways, parking areas, and other improvements within 15 feet of the easements. For underground facilities, demonstrate minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance per UCM § 1.10.5.
applicableAreas: All structures and improvements within 15 feet of electric easement boundaries
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 11 (Grading Plan), and Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). The site plan shows multiple buildings, driveways, and site improvements located near the recorded electric easements shown on the plat (Sheet 2). The grading plan (Sheet 11) displays easement boundaries using dashed lines (e.g., '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' P.U.E.'). However, NO dimensions or clearance measurements are provided between the easement boundaries and any proposed structures, driveways, parking areas, or other improvements. The vision analysis of the grading plan confirmed: 'There are **no notes or specifications** on this sheet that indicate...clearances from easement boundaries to structures.' Sheet 21 (electrical design) similarly shows transformer pad locations and underground electric lines but does NOT provide dimensioned clearances from the easements to nearby buildings or structures.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that easements be 'clearly delineated on plans' with 'surveys showing proximities.' The requirement for clearance verification exhibits is most critical when proposed structures are located within 15 feet of easement boundaries (15-foot radius clearance requirement per UCM § 1.10.3 for overhead distribution facilities; 5-foot horizontal clearance per UCM § 1.10.5 for underground facilities). This site has underground distribution facilities requiring 5-foot clearance minimums. The site plan demonstrates buildings, driveways, and parking areas in proximity to recorded easements, yet the plans provide NO exhibit showing dimensioned clearances from easement boundaries to these structures. Without these exhibits, compliance with clearance requirements cannot be verified. The burden of demonstrating compliance falls on the applicant—the absence of clearance verification constitutes a deficiency.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show existing electric easements with dimension callouts demonstrating clearances from easement boundaries to proposed structures. Provide dimensioned clearance details for all structures located within 15 feet of electric easement boundaries, showing that horizontal sky-to-ground clearance of 7.5 feet and 15-foot radius clearance from overhead conductors are maintained per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: All electric easement areas and proposed structures within 15 feet of easement boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts all buildings and easements but contains NO dimension callouts showing clearances from building structures to electric easement boundaries. Dimension callouts present only measure from buildings to overall property lines (e.g., Bldg 4 is 27.3' from east property line) rather than to the interior boundaries of adjacent electric easements. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) similarly shows easement boundaries but provides no dimensioned verification of clearances from structures. Facts.md documents that two critical easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement covering 0.31 acres in NE interior, and City of Austin Drainage Easement covering 0.130 acres in NE corner) are NOT depicted on the site plan, creating further ambiguity about clearance compliance. Multiple electric easements are shown (5' Electric Easements on east/south perimeter, 5' P.U.E., etc.) but no clearance verification exhibits with specific measurements demonstrating compliance with 15-foot clearance requirements for overhead facilities are provided.
findings.reasoning: The grouping requires clearance verification exhibits showing existing electric easements with dimensions from easement boundaries to proposed structures. The site plan adequately shows the location of buildings and easements, but affirmatively demonstrates NO clearance dimensions. While the site plan is otherwise complete, the absence of specific clearance callouts makes compliance verification impossible—the burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate clearance compliance, not on the reviewer to measure unmarked plans. This deficiency applies to all structures within 15 feet (for overhead facilities) of electric easement boundaries. Facts.md further documents that two major easements affecting the northeast corner are not depicted on submitted plans, which directly impacts the ability to verify clearances related to those undepicted easements.

findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits do not show existing electric easements with dimensions from easement boundaries to proposed structures. Easement boundaries are shown on the site plan but distances from easement boundaries to buildings are not dimensioned. Provide dimensional clearance exhibits showing distances from all electric easement boundaries to proposed structures, confirming minimum 15-foot clearance for overhead distribution facilities and 5-foot clearance for underground facilities.
applicableAreas: Site perimeter along property boundaries where electric easements are located
findings.observation: Examined Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21). Vision analysis confirms that buildings are dimensioned from property lines (e.g., Bldg 5 shown as 19.3' from top property line, Bldg 6 shown as 21.3' from right property line), but NO explicit clearance dimensions are drawn from easement boundaries to proposed structures. Electric and PUE boundaries are shown with dashed lines on the site plan, but distance from easement boundaries to buildings or structures is not dimensioned or verified. The easement boundaries are delineated but clearance verification is absent. Existing trees overlap OHE lines along the southern boundary.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that 'Easements are clearly delineated on plans, with surveys showing proximities' to structures. The deficiency here is that while easement boundaries are shown on the site plan, the specific clearance distances from those boundaries to proposed structures are not dimensioned or documented. For overhead distribution facilities requiring 15-foot clearance and underground facilities requiring 5-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.3, the applicant must provide explicit dimensional verification that clearances are maintained. The distance-to-property-line approach is insufficient because the easement boundaries may not align with property lines. Additionally, existing trees visible on the vision analysis overlap the OHE lines, indicating potential ground-to-sky clearance violations that further underscore the need for clearance verification exhibits.

findings.comment: 24/7 vehicular access to electric easements and facilities is not explicitly shown or dimensioned. Transformer pads are adjacent to internal driveways, but no formal access routes are designated. Please show and dimension access routes from the public right-of-way to all transformer pads and electric easements, with a note confirming 24/7 unobstructed access for maintenance vehicles and ensure gates or perimeter restrictions do not obstruct Austin Energy access.
applicableAreas: All electric easements on site, including transformer pad access routes
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9, 11, and 21 for explicit 24/7 vehicular access routes to electric easements and facilities. Sheet 21 vision analysis stated: 'Specific paved access routes dedicated solely to electrical facilities are **not shown or dimensioned**. Access appears to be assumed via the standard internal driveways that the facilities border.' The electrical design plan shows four transformer pads adjacent to internal driveways and parking areas, but NO explicit access route dimensions, no formal designation of which driveway serves which transformer, no 24-hour access provisions (gates, locks, or access permits noted), and no dimensions showing distance from pad to drivable surface. The grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show driveways and parking areas, but do NOT formally designate these as 'electric easement access routes' or provide any specification of 24-hour access requirements, width, surface type, or gate provisions. No notes on any sheet reference Austin Energy access rights or 24-hour access provisions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires 'permanent, unobstructed 24/7 vehicular access to all electric facilities for installation, operation, and maintenance.' This is a core requirement for all Austin Energy facilities. The grouping guidance identifies 'access shown but not dimensioned' as a common violation. While transformer pads are physically located near driveways, the site plan does NOT explicitly show or dimension access routes from the public right-of-way through the site to each facility, does NOT specify that these driveways provide 24/7 access, does NOT note any agreement with Austin Energy regarding access, and does NOT address what happens if site management restricts driveway access. Assumed access via adjacent driveways is insufficient; explicit, dimensioned, and labeled access routes from public ROW to each electric facility are required.

findings.comment: 24/7 vehicular access to electric easements and facilities on east and south boundaries is not provided from public right-of-way; access is obstructed by continuous concrete retaining wall and requires routing through private internal drives. Show explicit 24/7 maintenance access routes for all electric easements and facilities, with all-weather surface extending from public right-of-way, and dimension all clearances and route widths. Demonstrate that access does not require traversing private property or passing through gates/fencing without 24-hour key/lock provision.
applicableAreas: Electric easements on east and south property boundaries; all electric facilities requiring 24/7 access
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a continuous concrete retaining wall running the entire north, east, and south perimeter of the property, physically separating the interior townhome complex from the exterior easement areas. Vision analysis confirms: 'Easements running along the East and South boundaries appear entirely cut off from the public right-of-way (Valley View Road located on far west)... Accessing them from the street requires navigating through private internal drives, bypassing the townhome structures, and traversing the continuous Concrete Retaining Wall.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows NO explicitly labeled access routes (e.g., 'Electric Access Route' or 'Maintenance Path') designated exclusively for electric facilities. While transformer pads on the west side of the property are adjacent to the main driveway loop and are accessible, the 'Electric Easement' areas on the east and south perimeters, as well as pull boxes and other underground facilities in those areas, have no demonstrated access from public ROW. The plan notes 'No explicitly labeled maintenance paths or access routes designated for servicing the electric, telecom, or greenbelt utility easements.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 (Access to AE Facilities) and UCM § 1.14.4 (Access—Transmission Facilities) require that Austin Energy maintain permanent, unobstructed 24/7 vehicular access to all electric facilities for installation, operation, and maintenance. The defining requirement is that access must be available from public right-of-way without traversing private property or encountering physical obstructions. The site plan affirmatively demonstrates that easement areas on the east and south are separated from public street access by a continuous retaining wall; access to these areas requires routing through private internal driveway systems and bypassing residential buildings. This configuration fails to provide the 'unobstructed' access required by code. Further, the plan contains no explicit access route designations for electric maintenance, leaving access provisions ambiguous. The grouping's common violation pattern identifies this exact deficiency: 'Access shown but not dimensioned' or 'no access route from public ROW is shown.'

findings.comment: 24/7 vehicular access to electric easements and facilities not provided or shown, including access routes from public right-of-way, or is obstructed by fencing, gates, security features, or other site improvements. Transformer pad detail is incomplete (noted as 'need to look up approp. detail'). Provide detailed access routes from public ROW and/or parking areas to all electric transformer pads and easements, with dimensions and surface specifications. Show how 24/7 access is maintained to all electric facilities, including provisions for gates, removable fencing, or other mechanisms that allow Austin Energy personnel access at any time. Clarify the status of the existing retaining wall and fence along the eastern easement boundary and confirm they do not obstruct utility access.
applicableAreas: Electric transformer pad locations; eastern property line easement area; site perimeter
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) and Site Plan (Sheet 9) confirms: (1) Two pad-mounted transformer pads are shown on the site, one on the west side and one on the east side. The plan note adjacent to the transformer pad states 'need to look up approp. detail,' indicating the access design is incomplete. (2) No dimensioned access routes are drawn from parking areas, public ROW, or driveways to either transformer pad. (3) Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows an 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced' and 'Wood Fence' running along the eastern property line where the electric easements are located, potentially obstructing access. (4) The General Notes (Sheet 3) specify that '24-hour access to electric facilities shall be maintained' and 'Vehicular access for Austin Energy trucks and equipment is always to be maintained within the easement,' but the site plan does not show how this requirement is being met. (5) No gates, lift gates, removable sections, or other 24/7 access provisions are noted on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires 'Truck access to AE Construction and Existing Facility Sites' and UCM § 1.14.4 addresses transmission access corridors with 24-hour access requirements. The regulatory overview specifies 'Standard distribution access: 12 feet minimum horizontal width, 16 feet vertical clearance' and 'All-weather surface definition: Hot mix asphaltic concrete (HMAC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement.' The applicant must demonstrate that maintenance vehicles can reach all electric facilities from the public ROW or parking areas. The incomplete transformer pad detail ('need to look up approp. detail') and the absence of dimensioned access routes are deficiencies. The existing retaining wall and fence shown on the eastern boundary where electric easements are located could obstruct access to those easements. Additionally, no notation of 24/7 access provisions (such as gates with AE locks) is shown, raising questions about access during off-hours.

findings.comment: Multiple trees and vegetation (site amenities) are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the electric easement boundaries to comply with UCM § 1.10.10.2.
applicableAreas: southern 5' electric easement
eastern 5' electric easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple tree symbols (circles with branching canopy patterns) drawn directly on or overlapping the dashed lines indicating the southern 5' electric easement and eastern 5' electric easement. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) further documents these tree placements with legend symbols 'M' (Mitigation Tree), 'PL' (Parking Lot Tree), and 'P' (Parking Buffer Point Tree) positioned in these same easement areas along the southern and eastern property boundaries. Trees are site amenities and landscape features. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed: 'Multiple tree symbols (circles with branching patterns) are drawn directly on top of and within the dashed boundaries of this easement along the southern property line. Tree and vegetation symbols are drawn between the eastern property line and 'Bldg. 6', sitting directly within the marked 5' easement space.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits structures within electric easements where 'only electric facilities are permitted ground to sky.' Trees are structures with above-ground canopies and below-grade root systems. Site amenities, including landscaping features such as trees, are explicitly prohibited in the code. The site plan depicts multiple trees directly within the southernnortheastern 5' easement areas, violating this prohibition. Trees also trigger irrigation requirements (landscaping cannot survive without water in the arid Austin climate), which then implicates tree maintenance access, fertilization, and potential pruning—all activities that would further obstruct Austin Energy's access rights.

findings.comment: Concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond is a site amenity structure located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be removed or relocated outside the easement. No site amenities or structures other than electric facilities are permitted within electric easements.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed the concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement. Sheet 16 (Pond Details) shows the retaining wall is a concrete structural element with top elevation at 681.00. The checklist defines site amenities as 'signage, retaining walls, bike racks, street furniture, benches, dumpsters, light poles, or vertical structures.' A concrete retaining wall is explicitly listed as a prohibited site amenity within electric easements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and § 1.14.7 state: 'Site amenities including signage, retaining walls, bike racks, street furniture, benches, dumpsters, light poles, or vertical structures located within electric easements where only electric facilities are permitted' are prohibited. The concrete retaining wall is a site amenity structure within the electric easement.

findings.comment: Overhead electric facilities are present on the site but are not designated with 'aerial electric easement' label; generic electric easement label used instead. Revise all easement labels for facilities showing overhead lines (marked -OHE-) to explicitly read 'Aerial electric distribution easement' on all affected sheets, with appropriate width designation.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities and associated easements on north, east, south, and west perimeter of site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) vision analysis identified that overhead electric facilities are present on the perimeter, denoted by dashed lines with '-OHE-' notation (standard symbology for Overhead Electric). However, these same facilities are labeled with generic 'Elec. Easement' terminology without the 'aerial' designation. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) similarly does not distinguish between overhead and underground facilities in its easement labels. The electrical design plan shows 'Underground Electric Line' labels for proposed subsurface facilities within the development, but existing overhead facilities on the perimeter are not designated as 'Aerial electric easement.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.24 requires Austin Energy to obtain easements adequate for safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access. The regulatory overview in the grouping emphasizes that 'Plans must explicitly designate easements as aerial when overhead facilities are present—generic electric easement labels are insufficient.' The presence of overhead facilities (-OHE- notation) is confirmed on the plans, but the associated easements are not labeled to denote their aerial nature. This creates ambiguity regarding the clearance and access requirements applicable to the easement, as aerial and underground easements have distinct dimensional and operational requirements. The absence of 'aerial' designation obscures whether the easement width and clearance provisions accommodate overhead conductors and pole structures.

findings.comment: Overhead electric facilities not designated with 'aerial electric easement' label; generic electric easement label used instead. Overhead electric lines are present along the southern and western property boundaries but are not identified as 'aerial electric easement.' Revise all easement labels to include 'aerial' designation where overhead conductors or facilities are present, for example: 'Aerial electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement.'
applicableAreas: Southern and western property boundaries where overhead electric (OHE) lines are located
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) reveals that overhead electric lines are depicted along the southern and western property boundaries, labeled as 'OHE' (Overhead Electric). The plans show these existing OHE lines running parallel to the property lines where electric easements are also delineated. However, the easement labels for these areas do not include the designation 'aerial electric easement.' Instead, the easements are labeled generically as '5' Electric Easement' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' without the 'aerial' designation required when overhead facilities are present.
findings.reasoning: The regulatory overview explicitly states: 'Plans must explicitly designate easements as aerial when overhead facilities are present—generic electric easement labels are insufficient.' UCM § 1.3.24 addresses 'Easements for Electric Distribution Facilities' and requires that easements accommodate safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access. UCM § 1.16.0 requires clear delineation. When overhead facilities are present, the easement must be labeled 'aerial electric easement' to distinguish it from underground electric easements and to communicate the vertical clearance requirements (16 feet minimum for access, 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance per UCM § 1.10.3) that apply to aerial facilities. Generic labeling fails to communicate these critical distinctions.

findings.comment: License agreement not submitted for fencing within AE electric easement. Submit license agreement reviewed and approved by Austin Energy Property Agents and AE Design prior to site plan approval. Agreement must address fencing maintenance, easement access provisions, and removal obligations if AE requires future access.
applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary
Fencing locations within electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 show wooden privacy fencing running along the eastern and northern property boundaries. The eastern fencing is located directly within or immediately adjacent to electric easements labeled on Sheet 9 as 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14' and on Sheet 11 as '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76.' No license agreement documentation is included in the provided site plan materials for improvements (fencing) located within AE easements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10 requires license agreements for landscaping, trees, encroachments, or construction activities within AE easements. Agreements must be reviewed and approved by both AE Property Agents and AE Design prior to site plan approval. Fencing is an encroachment within an AE easement. No evidence of a license agreement has been submitted with this site plan application.

findings.comment: Wood fence is located within or immediately adjacent to AE easement on the eastern property boundary, but no license agreement with AE Property Agents and AE Design is documented on the site plan. License agreement approval must be obtained and submitted for this fence installation within the AE easement.
applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence location
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a wood fence running along the eastern property boundary, labeled as adjacent to a 5' Electric Easement (Vol. 69, Pg. 14). This fence is located within or immediately adjacent to an AE easement that requires AE access for installation, maintenance, and repair of electric facilities. The site plan notes and general notes on Sheet 3 do not reference or indicate that a license agreement has been obtained from AE Property Agents and AE Design for this fence installation within the easement. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed fence placement directly along the easement boundary.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10 requires license agreements for landscaping, trees, encroachments, or construction activities within AE easements. These agreements must be reviewed and approved by both AE Property Agents and AE Design prior to site plan approval. The wood fence appears to constitute an encroachment or improvement within the AE easement. No license agreement is documented on the site plan, and the absence of this required coordination represents non-compliance with the license agreement requirement.

findings.comment: Construction details of fence not provided. Submit detailed fence construction drawings showing materials, dimensions, post spacing, footing details, and gate locations. Details must show fence design is compatible with AE easement access and clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Entire perimeter fencing
Eastern, northern, and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows wooden privacy fencing (H-6 symbol) running along the northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries. The sheet contains only the symbol callouts and legend definitions but provides NO construction details such as fence height, materials specifications, post spacing, footing depths, or assembly details. No reference is made to detail sheets or section drawings for the fence construction.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires construction details of fences when fencing is proposed near AE facilities. The fencing shown on this plan is in proximity to electric easements (Sheet 9 labels 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14' and Sheet 11 shows '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76'). Construction details are essential for AE Design to review and approve the fence installation method to ensure it does not damage or interfere with underlying utilities or easement access.

findings.comment: Fencing is proposed adjacent to AE electric easement on the eastern property boundary, but construction details and specifications are not provided. Provide detailed fence construction drawings including profiles, sections, materials, post spacing, and foundation details for AE Design review and approval.
applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence adjacent to AE easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts a wood fence running along the eastern property boundary, immediately adjacent to or within the 5' Electric Easement. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) references the same fence. Block 9 on Sheet 9 contains only a brief 'Fence Note' that addresses post hole installation in Critical Root Zones (CRZs), requiring hand-digging and mulch application. No construction details, material specifications, profile views, section drawings, or structural details are provided for the wood fence on any sheet reviewed (Sheets 9, 22-39).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires construction details of fences to be provided when fencing is proposed in proximity to AE facilities. The fence's location adjacent to an AE easement qualifies as proximity to AE facilities. The site plan provides only a note about CRZ post hole installation but no fence construction details. The absence of detailed fence construction documentation prevents AE Design review and preliminary approval as required by the code.

findings.comment: Profile plan and detail drawings of fence and existing utility facilities not provided for AE Design review. Submit fence profile sections and coordination drawings showing fence elevation relative to electric easement boundaries and any existing utilities. Obtain Austin Energy Design preliminary approval of fence installation method.
applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary fencing
Areas adjacent to electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 31 shows wooden privacy fencing at the property boundaries but contains only plan-view callouts. No profile plan or section drawings are provided showing the vertical relationship between the fence line and the underlying electric easement or utility facilities. Sheet 9 identifies that the eastern fencing is located within electric easement areas. No documentation indicates that AE Design has reviewed and provided preliminary approval of the fence/utility coordination.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires profile plan and detail drawings of fence and existing utility facilities be provided for AE Design review and preliminary approval when fence installation may affect or be near existing AE utilities. The fence shown is in electric easement areas (Sheet 9: 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14'; Sheet 11: '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76'). Profile plans showing vertical clearances and utility coordination are necessary for AE Design to confirm the fence design will not interfere with easement access or damage underlying facilities.

findings.comment: No profile plan or detail drawings are provided for the wood fence near the AE electric easement on the eastern boundary. Submit profile plan view showing fence alignment and easement boundary relationship, and provide section details showing fence construction, post spacing, materials, and clearances to AE facilities for AE Design review and preliminary approval.
applicableAreas: Eastern property boundary; wood fence and AE easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) both show a wood fence on the eastern property boundary adjacent to the 5' Electric Easement. Review of construction detail sheets (Sheets 22-28) shows only standard details for curbs, sidewalks, water infrastructure, wastewater, and storm drain features; no fence profile plan or detail drawings are provided. Sheet 38-39 contain retaining wall details but not fence details. No profile plan view or section views of the fence and adjacent AE easement/facilities are present.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires profile plans and detail drawings of fences and existing utility facilities when fence installation may affect or be near existing AE utilities. These drawings must be submitted for AE Design review and preliminary approval. The site plan is missing the required profile plan (showing fence alignment relative to the easement in plan view with elevation references) and detail sections (showing fence dimensions, materials, post placement, and relationship to the underlying easement).

findings.comment: Underground electric line extends across southern property boundary to adjacent property without documented easement from adjacent owner or unified development designation per UCM § 1.3.8
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary; cross-property underground electric line extension to adjacent southern property

documentReferences.label: Master Comment Report - Electric Review (UCM § 1.3.8 referenced)

findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) explicitly identified: 'A blue Underground Electric Line extends southward from the Electrical Pull Box located south of Bldg. 7. This line explicitly crosses the heavy dashed main property line and extends into the adjacent property to the south, towards the offsite Elec. Easement.' The vision analysis confirms the line 'extends into the adjacent property to the south' without a documented easement label or recording reference on that neighboring property. The facts.md identifies the adjacent southern property owner information is not provided, and no easement instrument or unified development documentation is visible. The Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy is reviewing per UCM § 1.3.8 (Customer Electrical Facilities that Cross Property Lines), but no resolution or documented easement/unified development status is evident in the visible site plan materials.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.8 and Code § 15-9-123(B) establish that electrical facilities may extend across property lines ONLY under two conditions: (1) easements are obtained from the adjacent property owners, or (2) the properties qualify as a 'unified development.' Per the grouping guidance, unified development requires 'physical adjacency, common ownership, unified operation, and Austin Energy's determination,' and this status must be 'continuously maintained.' Facts.md shows different property owners (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC for the subject lot; no unified ownership indicated for the southern adjacent property). No easement from the southern property owner is documented on the site plan, and no unified development designation is stated. The presence of the off-site electric line without either an easement or unified development status constitutes non-compliance with UCM § 1.3.8 and Code § 15-9-123.

findings.comment: Show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan. Verify and document that no proposed trees or shrubs are located within transmission easement areas. If any trees currently exist within transmission easements, indicate their removal or obtain Austin Energy written approval.
applicableAreas: Electric transmission easement areas
findings.observation: The property plat (Sheet 2) and facts.md document record that electric easements exist on the property, including plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements. Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 20) explicitly states: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' However, the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show transmission easement boundaries, preventing verification that no trees are planted within transmission easements. Without visible easement boundaries overlaid on the landscape plan, compliance with the absolute prohibition on trees within transmission easements cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits all trees from being planted within electric transmission easements (facilities ≥60kV phase-to-phase). This is an absolute requirement with no exceptions based on tree size or species. The site plan notes on Sheet 3 reiterate this requirement. The applicant must show transmission easement boundaries on the landscape plan and demonstrate that no trees are positioned within them. The absence of easement boundaries on the landscape plan constitutes non-compliance with the documentation requirement.

findings.comment: Irrigation system layout deferred to as-built plan; specific sprinkler clearances from transmission structures within 25 feet not documented despite plantings shown within easement areas requiring irrigation.
applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries where electric easements are located; landscape planting zones
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts numerous trees within and immediately adjacent to the 5-foot electric easements along north, east, and south property boundaries. Trees are coded as 'SY' (Street Yard), 'PL' (Parking Lot), 'P' (Buffer Point), and 'M' (Mitigation) within or overlapping the utility line corridors. Sheet 31 guidance note states: 'Specific irrigation layout is not shown. The drawing does not visually map out sprinkler heads, lateral lines, or valves. Therefore, it cannot be visually confirmed if heads are placed within 25 feet of structures or easements. However...Given that plantings (which require water) are shown in these areas, it is highly likely irrigation infrastructure will be present near the utilities.' Sheet 31 (Irrigation Notes) defers specific irrigation system design to an as-built plan: 'THE IRRIGATION INSTALLER SHALL DEVELOP AND PROVIDE AN AS-BUILT DESIGN PLAN TO THE CITY.' No specific irrigation layout showing sprinkler clearances from transmission structures is provided on the landscape plan.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 14) state: 'Sprinklers are prohibited within 25 feet of transmission poles and structures.' Sheet 31 shows that significant plantings requiring irrigation are located within and immediately adjacent to transmission easements. The specific irrigation system layout, including sprinkler head locations and distances from transmission structures, is deferred to an as-built plan not included in this submittal. While it may be possible that the final irrigation design will comply with clearance requirements, the current plans do not affirmatively demonstrate compliance with the 25-foot prohibition. Approval cannot be granted without documentation showing that irrigation infrastructure will maintain required clearances.

findings.comment: Shrubs and tree plantings with mature canopies proposed directly within and overlapping 5-foot electric easements along north, east, and south property boundaries; will obstruct required access to transmission structure base during maintenance.
applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries within and adjacent to electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts multiple trees and shrubs (coded as 'SY', 'PL', 'P', 'M') positioned directly on or overlapping the 5-foot electric easement boundaries along the north, east, and south property lines. Specific vision analysis identified: 'North Boundary: Numerous large tree canopies (indicated by circles) are drawn directly on or overlapping this line and the property boundary'; 'South Boundary: Large tree canopies are drawn overlapping this area'; 'East Boundary: Tree canopies overlap the property line in this area.' These planted trees and associated shrubs will mature and create dense vegetation directly within and immediately adjacent to the transmission easements. Sheet 31 does not provide density, spacing, or height specifications that would allow verification that plantings will not obstruct access to structure bases during maintenance.
findings.reasoning: The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20, Item 1) explicitly state: 'Vehicular access for Austin Energy trucks and equipment is always to be maintained within the easement' and 'Shrubbery must not obstruct access to structure base' (UCM § 1.14.6). Sheet 31 shows plantings directly on/within the easement boundaries. These plantings, as they mature, will create obstacles to the 'walking or vehicle access to transmission structure base' that must remain clear per the grouping's regulatory overview. Mature tree canopies and shrub plantings within the easement violate this requirement.

findings.comment: Retaining walls and permanent site features (concrete fence, pond perimeter wall) proposed immediately at/within transmission easement boundaries along north, east, and south property lines; prevents required 25-foot level access corridor for maintenance vehicle turnaround.
applicableAreas: North, east, and south property boundaries; northwest and southwest corners where transmission structures located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) show retaining walls proposed immediately along the north, east, and south property boundaries where the 5-foot electric easements are located. Specific observations: North boundary retaining wall immediately adjacent to north easement; East boundary: 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced' and new concrete fence at east property line within/adjacent to easement; South boundary: concrete retaining wall running 'tightly along the southern property line, parallel and immediately adjacent to the southern OHE line and 5' Electric & Tele Easement.' The Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 20) specify a '25-foot access corridor' that must remain 'level' and free for Austin Energy maintenance vehicles. The site plan shows retaining walls and permanent features immediately at or within the transmission easement boundaries, eliminating any clear 25-foot access corridor for turnaround of 80,000-pound maintenance vehicles (Condor trucks) with 75-foot turning radius.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4 requires a '25-foot access corridor' along the entire length of transmission ROW, with 'Level access...designed to support 46,000-48,000 lb tandem axle loads' for Condor truck turnaround. The site plan's placement of retaining walls and permanent structures immediately at or within the transmission easement boundaries prevents the maintenance of this required corridor. The transmission facility access requirement (Condor truck turnaround with 75-foot turning radius) cannot be satisfied if permanent walls and features occupy the easement at property boundaries.

findings.comment: Existing overhead electric facilities are partially shown but not completely. Please add detailed callouts to identify all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, transmission voltage designations, and poles with cross-arm details and heights to all sheets showing existing overhead facilities.
applicableAreas: Site perimeter boundaries
valley view road frontage
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 4, 9, 21 for existing overhead facilities. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows existing overhead electric lines (OHE) and power poles along the perimeter, and there is a transformer on pad shown outside the property near Valley View Road. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows existing OHE lines on site edges with dashed line notation. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 21 reveals these are labeled as 'OHE' but specifics are limited: no callouts identify all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, or transmission lines explicitly. Guy wires are noted on Sheet 4 legend but unclear if shown for existing poles on this specific site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires all existing electric facilities to be shown, including 'poles, all three-phase conductors, neutral conductor, transmission lines, towers.' While existing overhead lines are depicted on Sheets 4 and 21, the plans do not provide explicit callouts or labels identifying: (1) all three phase conductors, (2) neutral conductor specifically, (3) transmission line voltage designation, or (4) detailed pole heights and cross-arm dimensions. The vision analysis found OHE lines but noted no detailed pole cross-sections or conductor specifications. This falls short of the 'completely shown' requirement in the deficiency title.

findings.comment: Landscaping in transmission areas not approved by AE transmission reviewer. Revise landscape plan to remove trees from transmission easement and 25-foot clearance zones around transmission structures. Obtain Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval of final landscape plan demonstrating compliance with 25-foot clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
Perimeter landscaping areas
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees planted along the southern boundary of the property in proximity to an overhead electric (OHE) line. The landscaping plan includes multiple tree planting symbols (large circles) positioned near this overhead electric facility. However, there are no clearance zone notations, no warnings, and no indication that Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval was obtained for this landscaping plan. No documentation of AE transmission review or approval is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires landscaping in transmission areas to be approved by Austin Energy transmission reviewer. Sheet 3 transmission notes explicitly state: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' The landscape plan shows tree plantings without documented compliance with these clearances or AE approval. Trees planted within clearance zones pose safety hazards and violate transmission protection requirements.
